summary: Implemented metadata-only renewal projection with independent calendar validity and review state, cumulative date windows, current scope context, and deduplicated first-gap accepted-evidence coverage.
public_contract: WorkspaceEvidenceRenewal and associated types are exported from @visua/core via packages/core/src/evidence-renewal.ts. The UI worker and lead were notified before service implementation.
behavior: GET /api/workspaces/:ws/evidence/renewal precedes evidence/:id, uses existing workspace.read authorization, and sends private/no-store.
Rows explicitly project safe metadata only; no content, data, blob handles, SHA or review history. Source metadata is never mutated.
Expired uses end<asOf; next7days and next30days are cumulative [asOf,asOf+window). Calendar expiry remains inclusive UTC day-end and exact expiry belongs to future windows.
Pending/rejected/unbound and future-collected records still receive finite date classifications; invalid/reversed dates and missing expiry remain outside date buckets with inspectable ids.

All recognized direct/group/out-of-scope links remain visible with context counts. Unknown links have a distinct count. Only current enabled, nonexcluded, nonwithdrawn, in-force, configured direct assessable scope enters impact.
Expired impact means currently uncovered direct requirements, independent of the expired artifact review state. No historical loss assertion is introduced.

Future impact follows accepted bound interval unions from now, accepts only gap-free future windows, stops at the first gap, treats reachable unbounded windows as no known loss, attributes rows to the terminal interval set, and deduplicates requirement counts.
No changes to attention, visua, scoring, evidence validation, schema, migrations, review or supersession behavior.

verification.command: pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/test/evidence-renewal.test.ts apps/server/test/evidence-renewal.test.ts packages/core/test/evidence.test.ts apps/server/test/attention.test.ts
verification.evidence: 4 files, 70 tests passed; duration 2.61s; SQLite in-memory server lane

Initial test tried to create a prohibited threat link via normal service and had an incorrect SOC2 fixture property. Replaced with deliberate legacy raw-store link fixture and reportType:type1. Final affected checks passed.

test_coverage: Core exact +/-1ms expiry, exact7/30d, UTC day-end/timezone normalization, all review states, future collection, invalid/reversed/missing windows.

Core alternate expiries, reordered rows, same endpoints, future bridge chains, one-millisecond adjacency vs actual gaps, indefinite alternative, pending/rejected/legacy/stale nonbridges, current uncovered.
Server expired pending/rejected semantics, multiple links dedupe, cumulative loss counts, matching ending rows, unreachable future starts, unbound acceptance.

Server current scope includes enabled/in-force role scope and excludes user exclusions, manual not-applicable, withdrawn, disabled, threat, future/ended/no-role laws, SOC categories, RMF baseline/tailoring; preserves context.

Server raw invalid/legacy dates, metadata-only with spies blocking hydrated reads and blob reads, unchanged workspace revision/audit, viewer access, foreign tenant404, unauthenticated401, cache header and fresh expiry transition.
limitations: PostgreSQL, production builds, browsers and full suites were not run by this worker; tests use existing backend-independent testDatabase fixture for the lead lanes.

Coverage projections assume unchanged current scope and recorded review/window metadata; they do not predict future collections, reviews, scope changes, legal applicability, implementation or verified status.

The existing scopeOf helper is reused unchanged; its law sunset uses the wall clock internally. Production endpoint captures current asOf, and tests freeze the clock. No historical scope API is provided.
Independent metadata reads match existing read-view behavior and do not claim a transactional historical snapshot.
Other workers edited their own files in the shared isolated worktree. This report owns only the six listed files; no commits or main application source edits were performed.
next_action: Lead copies/reviews the six owned files into integration when authorized, runs both database lanes and browser acceptance, and reconciles UI/docs wording with the public metadata contract.
